Upon success, the endpoint returns a JWT access token and refresh token for use in subsequent requests, encoding the user's id, role, and permissions as specified by requirements. This API operation is required as a system entry point for all standard users and is not used for any admin accounts or privilege escalation workflows.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a specific todo item for a given user. It operates on the todo_list_todos Prisma model, which is the core table for all user-managed task entities. The system enforces that users may only delete their own todos, while administrators have privileged rights to delete any todo as required. Deletion updates the soft delete timestamp ('deleted_at'), immediately excluding the todo from all standard user queries, but retaining the record for a potential undo window or auditing. This operation is strictly validated to check ownership: users cannot delete others' todos. All admin-initiated deletions trigger audit log entries capturing actor, timestamp, and affected resource. The deletion action does not remove the row from the database; instead, it sets the 'deleted_at' field in compliance with audit and retention requirements. Referential integrity, permission checks, and audit trails are all comprehensively enforced in this process.
operations.description:
Deletes a single todo item belonging to the authenticated user, or any user if performed by an admin.

If the operation is performed by a standard user, the system first verifies that the todo with the supplied ID is owned by that user and is not already deleted. Requests to delete a non-owned or already deleted todo result in a permission or not found error, respectively.

Upon successful permission check, the system handles the delete as a soft deletion by populating the 'deleted_at' timestamp. This ensures the todo is no longer included in active user lists, is hidden from all user-facing views, but retained for compliance and undo workflows. Admin actions trigger the creation of audit log entries to provide traceability for all privileged deletions.

The endpoint does not remove rows, preventing accidental loss of information, and enabling robust retention and regulatory audit policies. If an error occurs, the system provides clear error messages for permission denials, not found resources, or conflicts due to concurrent modification.

DTO containing authorized session information for the user after join, login, or refresh.

Returned from endpoints such as POST /auth/user/join, /auth/user/login, and /auth/user/refresh, this DTO provides essential identity and session data, including JWT tokens. Sensitive credentials and password hashes are strictly omitted in compliance with the security and privacy requirements.

email.description: Unique email address used for authentication. Must conform to RFC standards. Required to login.

password.description: Plaintext password for authentication. This value is never persisted or logged. Must meet minimum complexity requirements and is validated before login is permitted.

href.description: Connection URL of the login page. This is the URL from which the login attempt was made. Required for session context and security audit trails.

referrer.description: Referrer URL or the previous page visited by the client before the login attempt. Required for session context tracking and security analysis.

ip.description: Client IP address for security and session context. Optional: will be inferred by the backend if not provided by the client; provided in server-side rendering or proxy scenarios.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for authenticating an end user against the todo_list_users entity.

This DTO is used in login operations to receive credentials and necessary session information from clients attempting authentication. Includes email and password for credential validation, and connection context metadata (href, referrer, optional ip) for session creation, security auditing, and compliance. Email must match a registered, active account (deleted_at is null). Password is validated against securely stored hash. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are mandatory for self-login operations as per security policy.

Do not include any fields related to account role, ID, session token, or system attributes—authentication context is determined by business logic after credential validation.

refresh_token.description: Current refresh token value for the session renewal request. Submitted by the client; short-lived token issued at login, must be verified for authenticity and validity.

href.description: Connection URL where the refresh was requested. Captured for session tracking and audit purposes.

referrer.description: URL of the page from which the token refresh was initiated. Used for analyzing session flows and security investigations.

ip.description: Client IP address, optionally provided for session context and audit. If omitted, will be inferred by server.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body schema for refreshing a user's session in the Todo List application.

Used to submit a refresh token for session renewal and obtain new JWT tokens. Includes the refresh_token (short-lived, securely managed string) and session context fields (href, referrer, ip) for security auditing.

No credential fields are included—token verification and user status checks are handled by session middleware. Do not include user identity, authentication, or system fields outside of refresh_token and session context.

ITodoListAdmin.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for registering a new admin account for system management.

Fields correspond to the todo_list_admins Prisma table and are strictly validated for security and uniqueness. Used only for onboarding new admin users. Password is received in plain text for hashing during creation. Email and display_name must meet specified constraints and will be checked for uniqueness and valid format. Soft deletion and system fields are excluded from request; all are system-managed. Self-registering actors must provide session context (href/referrer required, ip optional).

email.description: Unique admin email for authentication. Must comply with RFC email format, and is globally unique among admin accounts.

password.description: Plain text password to be securely hashed. Never stored or transmitted except in hashed form; must meet defined security requirements.

display_name.description: Visible admin display/profile name used in logs and the admin UI. Must be 2–50 characters.

href.description: Connection URL (current page) where registration occurs. Required for session/audit trace.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page) for session/audit trace. Required for compliance and traceability.

ip.description: Client IP address at registration. Optional for self-registration; may be extracted server-side if omitted.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Response DTO for admin authentication: issued after join, login, or refresh.

Includes tokens and basic metadata for authenticated admin access. Used for credential lifecycle operations: join, login, session refresh. No sensitive internal security information is exposed. Conforms to security best practices for authentication responses. The token structure may reference additional JWT or session type components as needed; the id is always the admin uuid.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated admin from the todo_list_admins table.

email.description: Admin email address used for authentication. Always unique in the system.

display_name.description: Admin's display/profile name for identification in logs and UI.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601 format) indicating when the admin account was created in the system.

This field is set automatically and never changes, supporting audit trails and compliance requirements.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601 format) for the most recent profile or credential update to the admin account.

Reflects the last modification time, which advances on profile or security changes for auditing purposes.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the admin account was revoked, suspended, or voluntarily deleted.

Populated only for soft-deleted accounts; otherwise null. Used for security reviews and audit tracking.
No deletion has occurred (active account).

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the admin account was revoked, suspended, or voluntarily deleted.

Populated only for soft-deleted accounts; otherwise null. Used for security reviews and audit tracking.

session.description: Summary information for the active session context used for this authentication, referencing admin session table.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the admin account.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the admin record and is used to reference the account throughout the system. Guarantees uniqueness within the administrative user scope.

email.description:
Unique email address used to authenticate the admin.

Conforms to RFC email address format. Must be unique among all admins and serves as the primary credential for login and audit tracking.

display_name.description:
Display name of the admin.

A readable profile name, shown in audit logs and admin activity histories. Must be 2–50 characters.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of admin account creation.

Represents when the admin account was originally registered. Used for auditing, compliance, and administrative analytics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of last profile or credential update for the admin.

Indicates when any field (display name, credentials, etc.) was last modified.

ITodoListAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information for an administrative session/account.

Provides essential fields to identify and display admin actors in audit logs and privileged operation records. Does not include authentication credentials or sensitive fields. Used for list and reference embedding in session or activity-related APIs. Aligns with the todo_list_admins database schema; sensitive fields (like password) are excluded.

Use for lightweight summary of administrative identities and to track responsible parties in privileged operations.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description:
Request DTO for admin authentication.

Represents the input structure for an admin login attempt. Accepts the admin's registered email address and the plain password. Does not include session context fields, as session is established after successful login. Both fields are strictly validated against the admin table constraints, including unique email and password rule enforcement. Used exclusively for admin authentication endpoints, not for profile editing or registration.

email.description: Admin's registered email address for authentication. Must correspond exactly to a unique value in the todo_list_admins table. Validated against RFC standards. Required for login.

password.description: Admin's plain password submitted for credential verification. Never stored or logged in plaintext. Backend will hash and compare value using the stored password_hash in database.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Request DTO for admin session refresh.

Accepts the admin JWT refresh token for validating and renewing administrator authentication state. Used to extend or resume admin sessions in accordance with session and security policies. Field constraints are governed by the session model, and the provided refresh token is strictly validated before new authentication tokens are issued. No personal or credential data submitted; only the refresh token tied to the relevant admin session context is included. Used solely for admin session continuity, separate from login and registration operations.

refresh_token.description: The JWT refresh token linked to the current admin session. Used to request a new access/refresh token pair by verifying session validity and compliance with business rules.

id.description:
Primary key for the user account.

Represents the unique, system-generated identifier for each user in the Todo List application. All APIs and internal references use this value as the authoritative user reference. Must always be a valid UUID (RFC 4122 format), auto-generated at account creation.

Used to establish ownership for all user-created todos and session records. Never changes after initial creation.

email.description:
Email address used for authentication, must be unique and RFC compliant.

Every user account must have a unique email conforming to standard Internet email formats. This ensures reliable communication, account recovery, and unique login identity for each user.

The system enforces uniqueness and rejects attempts to register duplicate email addresses.

display_name.description:
User's visible profile name for display and personalization.

Used in all personal todo views, account screens, and optional sharing features. Length is enforced strictly between 2 and 50 characters to ensure usability and avoid display issues.

created_at.description:
Timestamp representing when the user account was first created (UTC ISO8601).

Immutable audit field, set automatically by the system at registration. Used for audit and compliance reporting, as well as for account age-based logic.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent change to the user's profile or credentials.

Automatically updated by the system whenever account data is modified. Used for history tracking, cache invalidation, and user notifications.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp for when the account was soft deleted; null if active or never deleted.

Soft deletion preserves user data for potential recovery or compliance audits instead of irreversible physical removal. A null value means the account is active. Only set by user-initiated deletion or administrative suspension.

ITodoListUser.description:
Represents a registered user account for the Todo List application.

Contains core identity and profile information such as unique email (for authentication), display name, account creation and update timestamps. Enforces strict data isolation—each user sees only their own profile and owned data. Used as the owner context for all personal todos and sessions.

Sensitive data such as the password hash is always excluded from API responses. All business logic, validation, and security controls are enforced according to requirements specified for the todo_list_users table.

email.description:
New email to set for this user account, must be unique and RFC compliant.

If specified, the API will validate that the email is unique and valid prior to applying the change. Used for login and notification; changing this triggers notification and may require re-verification.

Cannot be updated to match another user's email. Optional; only present if user is attempting to change their email address.

display_name.description:
New display name for this user, must be 2-50 characters.

Personalization field for the profile. If provided, replaces the user's current display name. API will strictly enforce minimum and maximum length constraints.

Optional; only present when user intends to change their visible name.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating editable profile fields of a registered user account in the Todo List application.

Allows self-service or admin-initiated changes to email or display name, with full internal validation according to the requirements of the todo_list_users table. System fields (id, timestamps, password hash, deletion status) are always excluded and cannot be updated through this DTO.

At least one property must be provided for the update operation to have effect; all properties are optional for PATCH/PUT compatibility.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Authentication session records for users.

Represents a single login or authentication event for a specific user. Tracks login context including IP address, connection URL, and referrer, as required for audit and compliance operations. Each session record is linked to its owning user's account and contains timestamps for creation and (if applicable) expiration.

Does not store tokens or device fingerprints, only connection metadata and time boundaries for strict regulatory audit requirements. Used in security review, login monitoring, and administrative audits. Managed as a subsidiary of the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session record. Automatically generated by the database. Used for referencing and deleting specific sessions.

todo_list_user_id.description: Reference to the owning user account (todo_list_users.id). Links this session to its parent user entity. Used for permission checks and audit traceability.

ip.description: IP address at login. Records the immediate network address used to authenticate this session for auditing and review purposes.

href.description: Connection URL at login. Captures the full page or endpoint through which login was initiated, supporting both audit/compliance and forensic analysis use cases.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at session start. Captures where the user was immediately prior to login, used for traceability and account security investigation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this session was created. Represents exact login time for compliance, security audits, and timeline reconstruction.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly ended. Nullable; may be null if session is still active.
Null if the session is currently active and has not expired or been explicitly ended.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired or ended, or null if still active.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Parameters for searching, filtering, or paginating authentication session records for a given user in the todo_list_user_sessions table.

Supports pagination (page, limit), filtering by date or status, and text search. Used for both user-facing and administrator access patterns. Designed to ensure search results remain within the authenticated user's permissions or under explicit admin supervision.

Applies strict filtering and sort parameters to support security, compliance, and usability requirements.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be greater than or equal to 1. Used to navigate multi-page result sets.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries per page to return. For performance reasons, must be between 1 and 100.

search.description: Optional text search applied to IP, href, or referrer fields. Case-insensitive. Returns all matching sessions for the user or admin actor.

from.description: Filter sessions created on or after this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format (date-time in UTC or Asia/Seoul).

to.description: Filter sessions created on or before this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format (date-time in UTC or Asia/Seoul).

oneOf.description: Filter by session status: 'active' for currently valid sessions (not expired), 'expired' for sessions that ended or timed out.
Filter by session status: 'active' for currently valid sessions (not expired), 'expired' for sessions that ended or timed out.

status.description: Filter by session status: 'active' for currently valid sessions (not expired), 'expired' for sessions that ended or timed out.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the administrative account. This is a primary key and is used as the global reference for distinguishing admin users across the Todo List system.

Assigned at account creation and immutable for the lifetime of the admin account. Used for audit logging, account management, and in path parameters for all admin-specific API requests.

email.description:
Unique email address used for administrator authentication and communication.

Must conform to email RFC standards and be unique among all admin accounts in the todo_list_admins table. Used as the login credential and for security/audit notifications.

display_name.description:
Visible profile name of the administrator, shown in audit logs and management UIs.

Must be between 2 and 50 characters. Used for identification in system logs, activity feeds, and dashboards.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601 format) indicating when the admin account was created in the system.

This field is set automatically and never changes, supporting audit trails and compliance requirements.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601 format) for the most recent profile or credential update to the admin account.

Reflects the last modification time, which advances on profile or security changes for auditing purposes.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the admin account was revoked, suspended, or voluntarily deleted.

Populated only for soft-deleted accounts; otherwise null. Used for security reviews and audit tracking.
No deletion has occurred (active account).

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the admin account was revoked, suspended, or voluntarily deleted.

Populated only for soft-deleted accounts; otherwise null. Used for security reviews and audit tracking.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Administrator account entity for Todo List system-wide management and oversight.

Represents privileged user identity for auditing, system configuration, and enforcing business rules. Admin accounts are uniquely identified by UUID and managed via secure email/password authentication. Certain fields (such as password hash) are never included in responses for security reasons.

This schema provides all necessary information for privileged platform APIs, compliance audits, and admin dashboards while preserving privacy boundaries for authentication credentials.

email.description: New unique email address for the administrative account, if updating. Must be RFC-compliant and not currently used by another admin. Used in authentication and as a contact point for system notifications.

display_name.description:
New profile display name for the administrator.

Must be between 2 and 50 characters if provided. Used for identification in system audit logs and dashboards.

oneOf.description: Set this field to a timestamp to soft-delete (revoke/suspend/terminate) the account. The backend may use this for compliance actions or voluntary resignations.
Clear prior deletion (restore account) or explicitly show as not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp to mark the admin account as soft-deleted (revoked/suspended) if set. Value should be ISO 8601, or null.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Request body to update administrator accounts in the Todo List platform.

Fields are all optional and only those provided will be updated. Ownership, account creation and password hash/credentials cannot be changed through this DTO. Used only by privileged admin actors in authenticated system management APIs.

Audit tracking and security policies are enforced on every update; attempts to modify restricted or non-editable fields will result in errors. Password modification must use a dedicated endpoint, not this DTO.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin session record. This value serves as the primary key and is generated as a UUID following open standards.

ip.description: IP address at session start. Used for audit, location analysis, and security policies.

href.description: Connection URL used by the admin at login. Captures the environment from which access originated, useful for auditing and trace.

referrer.description: Referrer URL for audit traceability. Stores the URL the admin navigated from when logging in, supporting session context and compliance investigation.

created_at.description: Timestamp for session creation. Records when the admin session was first authenticated and is set automatically at login.

expired_at.description: Timestamp for session expiration or manual termination. Null if the session is currently active, otherwise records the end of session lifetime.

admin.description: Reference to the administrator associated with this session. Contextual information for audit and privilege review, always provided as a summary type for efficient inclusion.

ITodoListAdminSession.description:
Authentication session records for administrators.

Each record represents a single login session for an admin account, including IP, connection URL, and referrer details for compliance and security auditing. Sessions enable tracing of every admin action to an authenticated session and identity. Expiration datetime supports scheduled or manual logout. Multiple concurrent sessions are allowed for administrative flexibility. All privileged system operations are executed in the context of a session in this table. No personal data beyond session context and actor reference is stored here.

page.description: Current page number (1-based) for paginated results. Defaults to 1 if unspecified.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records per page. Typical default is 20. Upper bound set to prevent excessive data retrieval.

oneOf.description: Field by which session records are sorted. Limited to sortable timestamp fields for audit purposes.
Field by which session records are sorted. Limited to sortable timestamp fields for audit purposes.

sort_by.description: Field by which session records are sorted. Limited to sortable timestamp fields for audit purposes.

oneOf.description: Sorting direction for results: ascending or descending.
Sorting direction for results: ascending or descending.

sort_order.description: Sorting direction for results: ascending or descending.

created_from.description: Filter: include only sessions created on or after this RFC 3339 timestamp.

created_to.description: Filter: include only sessions created on or before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

expired_from.description: Filter: include only sessions expired on or after this RFC 3339 timestamp. Supports null for active sessions.

expired_to.description: Filter: include only sessions expired on or before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

ip_like.description: Filter: include only sessions where IP address contains this substring or pattern. Supports audit and security use cases.

referrer_like.description: Filter: include only sessions where referrer URL contains this substring or pattern.

ITodoListAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for restricting admin session records.

Supports pagination, sorting, and advanced filtering fields to enable security and compliance review of all authentication session records associated with a given administrator. All filters are optional and may be combined for complex queries. Used by privileged operations for audit, incident response, and periodic compliance reviews in the administration portal.

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrative account for system management and oversight.

Represents only core attributes of administrative actors engaged in privileged actions, such as audit log entries, system configuration, or user oversight. This schema is used as a lightweight reference in contexts where only identification and display information are required, not full profile or credential data.

Linked to the audit log entity for provenance tracking and incident forensics. Each summary object provides unique identification, authenticated email, and the administrator's profile name, as recorded in audit events and privilege assignment workflows.

id.description: Unique admin identifier. Matches the primary key in the todo_list_admins table.

email.description: Admin's login email address, used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique among all admins and conform to RFC standards for email validation.

display_name.description: Visible administrator profile name, shown in audit log records, privileged system notifications, and the administrative dashboard. Must be 2–50 characters, consistently linked to actions performed by this admin in the system database and logs.

id.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the todo item.

title.description: Short title of the todo item. Must be 1–100 visible UTF-8 characters, unique per user among non-deleted todos. Stripped of leading/trailing whitespace.

oneOf.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. May be null or empty, up to 1000 characters.
Description is omitted or not present.

description.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. May be null or empty, up to 1000 characters.

oneOf.description: Todo status in business workflow. Allowed values: 'pending', 'completed'. Only these two values are valid in minimal version; future states can be added with migration.
Todo status in business workflow. Allowed values: 'pending', 'completed'. Only these two values are valid in minimal version; future states can be added with migration.

status.description: Todo status in business workflow. Allowed values: 'pending', 'completed'. Only these two values are valid in minimal version; future states can be added with migration.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed. May be null if not completed.
Completion has not yet occurred.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed. May be null if not completed.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp of the todo item. Set when the record is first created.

updated_at.description: Last modification timestamp. Updated on every change of title, description, or status.

oneOf.description: Timestamp for soft deletion. Null if the todo is not deleted; set when user deletes for retention/undo window.
Todo is not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if the todo is not deleted; set when user deletes for retention/undo window.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Main todo item entity for personal task management.

Represents an individual user-owned task, supporting the full lifecycle from creation, update, completion, to (soft) deletion. Each todo belongs exclusively to one authenticated user and is never visible to others except admins. The entity supports fast retrieval, multi-field filtering, case-insensitive searching, and provides all audit and business timestamps required for compliance and lifecycle tracking.

Field structure enforces domain rules: only non-deleted todos may share the same title for a user, completion is timestamped, and filtered list views are optimized by indexes. Temporal fields (created_at, updated_at, completed_at, deleted_at) allow robust retention, undo, and audit patterns as needed by the product.

Foreign keys, constraints, and indexes ensure data integrity and high query performance for typical CRUD and search operations.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Criteria object for advanced filtering, searching, and pagination of a user's todo items in task list retrieval operations.

This DTO is not directly mapped to any database table or persistent domain entity; it serves as the API request body for complex query and list search actions. Each property is optional and allows clients to compose sophisticated operations including full-text search, field-based filtering, sorting, and pagination controls.

The structure is extensible for future requirements, and edge cases of field combinations—such as supplying both full-text query and status filter, or omitting all filters for an unconstrained fetch—are fully supported. Maintain API contract discipline when extending this type: new properties must maintain backward compatibility for clients and ensure the same semantics for omitted and null values.

All filtering and pagination logic is handled by the backend, which interprets property presence, absence, or null values according to the business logic described in requirements analysis.

Not mapped directly to any persistent entity.

query.description: Full-text search expression for the todo title or description. If omitted, results are not filtered by content.

oneOf.description: Only include todos with a status of 'pending' in the results.
Only include todos with a status of 'completed' in the results.

status.description: Constraint to only include todos with the specified status. Omit for no status filtering.

created_from.description: Include todos created at or after this ISO 8601 datetime (as per RFC 3339). Optional; omit for no lower bound.

created_to.description: Include todos created before or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime (as per RFC 3339). Optional; omit for no upper bound.

completed_from.description: Include todos completed at or after this ISO 8601 datetime (as per RFC 3339). Optional; omit for no lower bound.

completed_to.description: Include todos completed before or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime (as per RFC 3339). Optional; omit for no upper bound.

oneOf.description: Sort results by creation timestamp (default).
Sort results by update timestamp.
Sort results by completion timestamp.
Sort results lexicographically by title.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'completed_at', 'title'. If omitted, defaults to 'created_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort in ascending order.
Sort in descending order (default).

sort_order.description: Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). If omitted, defaults to 'desc'.

page.description: 1-based page number for paginated results. Optional; defaults to 1.

page_size.description: Number of records per results page. Optional; default is 20, maximum is 100.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new todo item.

This structure allows clients to specify a short title as a required task identifier and optionally provide an extended description, subject to length limits and unique-per-user constraints. Titles are strictly enforced as unique among all of a user's non-deleted todos, must be 1–100 visible UTF-8 characters, and are trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace. The optional description supports up to 1000 characters, can be omitted entirely, or explicitly provided as null; the backend must recognize the distinction for validation and storage simplicity.

Ownership attribution is server-enforced: the new todo is always attributed to the currently authenticated principal, and this cannot be overridden by the request body.

System-managed fields (status, created_at, updated_at, completed_at, deleted_at, as well as the foreign key to the owning user) are exclusively set by the backend and must not appear in the request. Attempts to supply these fields should be rejected or safely ignored according to the API's error handling policy.

Validation occurs at both API and persistence layers, with business rules for field uniqueness, required/optional distinction, and maximum length enforced end-to-end.

title.description: Short title of the todo item. Required and must be unique for the authenticated user's active (non-deleted) todos. 1–100 UTF-8 characters, stripped of whitespace; cannot be empty or whitespace-only after trimming.

oneOf.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. May be provided as a string (up to 1000 characters), omitted entirely, or set to null. If omitted or null, no description will be stored.
Indicates that no description is being set for this todo. The backend recognizes the absence of a description.

description.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. Maximum 1000 characters. The property may be omitted, explicitly set to null, or contain a textual value. System logic should handle each case accordingly.

title.description: Short title of the todo item. If provided, must be 1–100 visible UTF-8 characters, unique per user among non-deleted todos.

oneOf.description: Extended description of the todo item. Up to 1000 characters.
Description to be cleared or absent.

description.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. Up to 1000 characters.

oneOf.description: New status of the todo. Allowed values: 'pending' or 'completed'. Status change will set or clear completed_at as appropriate.
New status of the todo. Allowed values: 'pending' or 'completed'. Status change will set or clear completed_at as appropriate.

status.description: New status of the todo. Allowed values: 'pending' or 'completed'. Status change will set or clear completed_at as appropriate.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for a todo item.

Allows updating the title, description, or status of a todo. Title must remain unique among active todos for the user and 1–100 UTF-8 characters if given. Description can be set (up to 1000 characters), removed (null), or left unchanged. Status must be either 'pending' or 'completed'; business logic ensures proper update of related fields. System-controlled timestamps, completion, and ownership are always handled by the backend; only mutable fields are present here. All fields are optional; if omitted, value remains unchanged.

ITodoListAuditLog.description:
System audit log entry for privileged administrative events and compliance tracking.

Represents a single, immutable log capturing a sensitive administrative action or compliance event within the Todo List application. Each entry includes the administrative actor, potentially affected target user, event category, timestamp, and optional narrative. Used for forensics, legal compliance, and to support investigation workflows. Audit entries cannot be changed or deleted.

Foreign keys reference admin and user tables for traceability. Optimized for search and filter on actor, timestamp, event type, and details. Populated only by the system, never by clients.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for each audit event.

admin.description: Administrator responsible for the event. Actor reference for traceability to system admin.

target_user.description: (Optional) User account affected by the event. If present, references the user entity; otherwise null.

event_type.description: Type/category of the event (e.g., 'user_deletion', 'todo_removed', etc.). Short, machine-readable string.

event_time.description: Precise UTC ISO8601 timestamp for when the event occurred.

details.description: Optional narrative/context for the event (max 2000 chars). Provides business reason, who, what, and why for this privileged event.

ITodoListAuditLog.IRequest.description:
Filter criteria and pagination/sorting parameters for searching audit logs.

Allows filtering by event_time (range), event_type (exact matches), administrator (by ID), affected user (by ID), and keyword search in details narrative. Pagination controls and sorting options enable efficient review of large audit log volumes. Only accessible to admin users.

event_time_range.description: Restricts log results to those within this UTC date-time range. Null for no restriction.

event_types.description: If present, only include specific event types/categories. Array of machine-readable event_type strings.

admin_id.description: If specified, restricts to logs authored by a single admin. UUID referencing admin table. Null for no restriction.

target_user_id.description: If specified, restricts to logs affecting the specified user. UUID referencing user table. Null for no restriction.

search.description: Full-text search keyword for the details field.

page.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Page size (number of entries per page). Defaults to 20, max 200.

sort_descending.description: If true, results are ordered by most-recent event_time first (descending). Defaults to true.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an end user whose account may be affected by privileged or compliance events. This type is referenced by audit log entries for traceability.

Contains only identifying information necessary for review and investigations, not authentication or full profile fields.

display_name.description: User's display name for UI and logs.

IDateTimeRange.description:

System-wide application configuration and global settings object.

Provides a centralized representation for storing key/value pairs, flags, and operational parameters used by the todo list application at runtime. Each object represents a distinct configuration setting and is mapped directly to a row in the todo_list_system_settings Prisma table.

ITodoListAuditLog.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a system audit log entry for privileged administrative events and compliance tracking.

Provides concise information about an audit event, listing its actor (administrator), event category, affected target, main time, and a minimal narrative for administrative review, compliance reporting, or quick filtering. Serves as a lightweight alternative to the full audit log record, optimized for list display and reporting scenarios.

Intended for use cases such as audit history lists, compliance dashboards, and search/filtering endpoints. Contains only essential attributes for quick reference, omitting full context and large text detail fields.
